post.summary: Create a GitHub issue from a conversation
post.description: Opens an issue with exactly this title and body in the connected repo, and links it to the conversation. Only title and body are sent: no labels, assignees or milestones. The body ends with an HTML comment GitHub doesn't show, `<!-- helpdesk-claim:<id> -->`, so that if GitHub's answer is lost (a timeout, a 5xx) the server can find exactly this issue instead of opening a duplicate. When the issue is closed as completed, the conversation gets a `fixed` draft to approve. One issue per conversation. Needs `conversations:read` and `github:write`.

post.description: Called by GitHub with the connected repo's `issues` events. `?workspace=` names the workspace; `X-Hub-Signature-256` must be the HMAC of the body with that workspace's webhook secret. Conversations are matched by the event's repo and issue number, so issues made while another repo was connected still close, as long as that repo's webhook has the current secret. When an issue linked to conversations is closed as completed, each conversation gets a `fixed` draft for a human to approve. A delivery for an issue already closed changes nothing, so a replay is harmless. Other events are acknowledged and ignored.
